62:                 "signal storage was not initialized",
63:             ));
64:         }

67:         let sender_fd = globals.sender.as_raw_fd();
68:         if receiver_fd < 0 {

288:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
289:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.

291:         Handle {
292:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
293:         }
294:     }

296:     fn process(&self) {
297:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
298:         //
299:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
300:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
301:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
302:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
303: 
304:         let ev = match self.receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
305:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
306:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
307:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
308:         };
309: 
310:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
311:         // if another signal has come in.
312:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
313:         loop {
314:             match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf) {
315:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
316:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
317:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
318:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
319:             }
320:         }
321: 
322:         self.receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
323: 
324:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
325:         globals().broadcast();
326:     }
327: }

part.text:
Fixed by removing the spurious `WRITABLE` interest registration in the Unix signal driver (tokio/src/signal/unix/driver.rs:230). The self-pipe receiver is never written to by the driver, so writable interest serves no purpose and causes a spin loop with level-triggered selectors (e.g. `poll`-based) where the descriptor is always writable.

Verification:
- All 10 signal test binaries pass (`signal_ctrl_c`, `signal_usr1`, `signal_drop_*`, `signal_multi_rt`, `signal_no_rt`, `signal_notify_both`, `signal_panic`, `signal_twice`)
- `rt_basic`, `rt_common`, `process_kill_on_drop`, `io_driver` pass — except 3 pre-existing `io_notify_while_shutting_down` failures that fail identically on the unmodified baseline due to a container network limitation (`AddrNotAvailable`), unrelated to this change.
